newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse heavyweights keep turnover high.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse heavyweights keep turnover high.

text.p: Heavy trading on the first tier of the Bucharest stock exchange kept turnover high at 2.02 billion lei on Wednesday, close to the previous session's level of 2.2 billion.
Azomures SA fertiliser maker and chemical plant Oltchim, the only two first-tier listings of the 23 traded stocks, took more than 95 percent of turnover.
"We expected turnover to stay high, but we did not see it topping 2.0 billion lei, with sessions so close to each other," said a trader.
Wednesday trading was introduced for the first time this week, taking to three the number of weekly sessions on the bourse.
"For the first time in a long time Azomures failed to take the bulk of trading, performing in the shadow of Oltchim due to selling pressure and lower demand," another trader said.
Azomures had a turnover of 641.1 million lei and shed 20 lei to close at 1,610.
Oltchim closed 20 lei stronger at 1,650. Most other prices drifted higher in low supply and five stocks had no trade.
Two independent indices fell for the first time since early January, on the back of lower average prices of Azomures and Oltchim, which account for the bulk of market capitalisation.
Newcomer AMEP SA, a food package company, put on a good show for its first day of trading with a volume of more than 17,000 shares on turnover of 20.4 million lei, traders said.
Brokers said a change in the reference price floating corridor to plus/minus 50 percent from 10 percent had managed to unblock trading in several stocks.
"The most clear case was that of Feleacul, whose average price rose by 50 percent," said a broker.
Feleacul confectionery maker closed at 1,320 -- which was also its average price -- up from 880 on Tuesday.
The two unofficial indices -- the VAB and the BIG -- fell by 0.8 and 0.38 percent respectively from the previous session.
